content: Triamterene is a medication that can be used on its own or in combination with other drugs to treat edema, which is the retention of excess fluid in body tissues. This condition can arise from various causes, including liver or heart disease. Triamterene belongs to a class of drugs known as diuretics, commonly referred to as water pills. It works by prompting the kidneys to remove unnecessary water and sodium from the body through urine while minimizing the loss of potassium. Triamterene is available in capsule form and is taken orally. It is typically taken once daily in the morning after breakfast or twice daily after breakfast and lunch. To avoid disruptions to nighttime sleep caused by frequent urination, it is recommended to take this medication earlier in the day. It is important to take Triamterene at the same time(s) each day and to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions or concerns, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more or less of the medication or take it more frequently than prescribed. Triamterene is also used in combination with other diuretics to manage high blood pressure. It may be prescribed for other purposes as well; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before taking Triamterene, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication or any other drugs, including Dyazide or Maxzide. Do not take Triamterene if you are already taking amiloride (Midamor), spironolactone (Aldactone), or other medications containing Triamterene. Provide your doctor and pharmacist with a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take. Be sure to mention ACE inhibitors (e.g., benazepril, captopril, enalapril, lisinopril), lithium, NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen), diabetes medications, blood pressure medications, other diuretics, and potassium supplements. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had diabetes, gout, kidney stones, or heart, kidney, or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or become pregnant while taking Triamterene, notify your doctor immediately. Do not breastfeed while taking this medication. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking Triamterene. Avoid unnecessary or prolonged exposure to sunlight, and wear protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen, as Triamterene may increase your skin's sensitivity to sunlight. Follow your doctor’s dietary recommendations, which may include a low-sodium diet and a daily exercise program. Be mindful of potassium-rich foods (e.g., bananas, prunes, raisins, orange juice) in your diet. If you miss a dose of Triamterene, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Triamterene may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience vomiting, dizziness, or headache, especially if these symptoms persist or worsen. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention and include muscle weakness or cramps, slow or irregular heartbeat, diarrhea, rash, difficulty breathing or swallowing, upset stomach, extreme tiredness, unusual bleeding or bruising, lack of energy, loss of appetite, pain in the upper right part of the stomach, yellowing of the skin or eyes, flu-like symptoms, sore throat, severe dry mouth, or unusual bruising or bleeding. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store Triamterene in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Symptoms of overdose may include upset stomach, vomiting, weakness, tiredness, or dizziness. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as they may order tests to monitor your body’s response to Triamterene. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
